source_block.parva: Drona Parva · fifteenth day (afternoon) · Narayanastra-mokshana upaparva
source_block.bori: BORI CE Drona Parva (Narayanastra-mokshana upaparva), Debroy translation vol. 6–7: Ashvatthama learns from Kripa how Drona laid down arms on the lie; vows vengeance; tells Duryodhana of the Narayana weapon (Narayana's boon to Drona, passed to his son); invokes it — arrows, iron balls, discs and maces of fire; it grows wherever it is resisted; Yudhishthira despairs; Krishna orders all to drop weapons and alight; Arjuna refuses to use Gandiva against it; Bhima alone resists with his mace and the weapon gathers on him; Krishna and Arjuna drag him down and disarm him; the weapon is pacified; Duryodhana asks again; Ashvatthama says it cannot be used twice.
source_block.gita_press: Gita Press Gorakhpur Mahabharata (Hindi, Drona Parva, Narayanastra-moksha parva): same sequence — Ashvatthama's grief and vow, the Narayanastra, Shri Krishna's counsel to lay down arms and descend from vehicles, Bhimasena's resistance and forcible disarming, the weapon stilled, and its single use.
source_block.ganguli: K.M. Ganguli, Drona Parva §193–201 (vulgate; Narayanastra-mokshana): Aswatthaman hears of his sire's death (§193); his vow and the weapon's origin (§195–196); Arjuna/Satyaki/Dhrishtadyumna quarrel (§197–199, omitted); invocation, Yudhishthira's lament, Vasudeva's counsel, Bhima's refusal, Arjuna's Gandiva vow (§200); Varuna weapon over Bhima, Krishna and Arjuna drag him down, pacification, 'cannot be used twice' (§201).
source_block.divergence: Chapter numbers differ between BORI CE and the vulgate (Ganguli/Gita Press). Ganguli's vulgate has Arjuna also cover Bhima with the Varuna weapon before he and Krishna drag Bhima down; this detail is not depended on here (not narrated, not drawn). source_block.chosen: Gita Press + BORI/Debroy overlap: the Narayanastra, Krishna's counsel to disarm and dismount, Bhima's resistance and forcible disarming by Krishna and Arjuna, the pacification, and the weapon's single use. Ganguli for English wording.
source_block.notes: Not TV. Comic-mythology only; no gore — the weapon is golden fire in the sky; no bodies are shown or narrated. Drona is narrated only (never drawn). Ashwatthama = new 3:2 lock with the forehead jewel as his token. Krishna = Ep 09 look lock; Arjuna = Ep 09 face, cream-white dhoti, no gold armor/peacock (Ep 14 lock / A4). Yudhishthira and Bhima = Ep 14 locks; Duryodhana = Ep 13 lock. Never attach Ep01 plate-wide-gold or any finished plate as an Imagine ref. Bhima/Dushasana (Karna Parva) is not in this episode.
